findings.title: No visible authentication/authorization check on project access
findings.explanation: The handler returns all events for any projectId without verifying the caller is allowed to access that project. If the router-level middleware doesn't enforce per-project membership, this is an IDOR exposing the full activity log (including payloads) of any project. Confirm the JSON events endpoint's access check is applied here (shared middleware or a helper) and add a test for a user without access getting 403/404.

findings.title: CSV injection (formula injection) not mitigated
findings.explanation: `kind` is written unescaped and the payload is user-controlled data. Cells beginning with =, +, -, @, tab or CR will be executed as formulas when opened in Excel/Sheets. Since this file is meant for customers to open in spreadsheets, prefix such values with a single quote (or otherwise neutralize them) after CSV-escaping.

findings.title: Incorrect CSV escaping: `kind` is not quoted and payload is double-stringified
findings.explanation: `kind` is emitted raw, so any comma, quote or newline in it corrupts the row structure. The payload uses `JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(...))`, which produces a JSON string literal with backslash-escaped quotes (`"`), not RFC 4180 escaping (`""`). Parsers will mis-read the column and the data will not round-trip. Write a small `csvEscape(value)` helper that converts to string, doubles internal quotes, and wraps in quotes when the value contains `,`, `"`, `\n` or `\r`, and use it for every field with `JSON.stringify(payload)` as input for the payload column. Prefer a vetted library (e.g. csv-stringify).

findings.title: Unbounded in-memory load of 10,000 rows with large JSON payloads, no streaming
findings.explanation: `pool.query` buffers all rows (payload size is unbounded) in memory per request, and `res.write` ignores backpressure. A few concurrent exports can spike memory and block the event loop. Use a cursor/`pg-query-stream` piped to the response (or at least respect backpressure with `drain`), and consider rate limiting this heavy endpoint.

findings.title: projectId is not validated
findings.explanation: `Number(req.params.projectId)` yields NaN for non-numeric input (and accepts values like `1.5`, `''`->0, `1e3`). NaN gets passed to Postgres and results in a 500 or driver error. Validate with `Number.isInteger(projectId) && projectId > 0` and return 400 otherwise.

findings.title: No error handling for async handler
findings.explanation: If the query throws, Express 4 will not catch the rejected promise, leading to an unhandled rejection and a hung request. Wrap in try/catch or use the project's async wrapper. Additionally, once `res.write` has begun, errors can't produce a clean status code, so handle mid-stream failures (destroy the response) deliberately.

findings.title: Missing project existence / archived handling
findings.explanation: A nonexistent project returns 200 with just a header row, and archived projects (soft-deleted via `archived_at`) are exported without any check. Decide the intended behavior and return 404 for missing/archived projects consistent with the JSON endpoint.

findings.title: Duplicated query and silent truncation
findings.explanation: The description says this is the same query as the JSON endpoint with a larger limit, but the SQL is copy-pasted. Extract a shared query function with a limit parameter to prevent drift. Also, customers asking for 'the activity log' silently get only the latest 10,000 events; consider documenting this, adding a truncation indicator, or supporting date-range filters/pagination. Also, `id DESC` ordering means the newest events come first; confirm this is desired for an export.

findings.title: Column order and header mismatch with data semantic; created_at assumes Date
findings.explanation: Header and values are aligned currently, but `row.created_at.toISOString()` throws if the column is null or the pg type parser returns a string (e.g. custom type parsers or `timestamp` configurations). Verify the column is NOT NULL and returns Date, or guard accordingly.

findings.title: Content-Type lacks charset; no BOM for Excel
findings.explanation: Use `text/csv; charset=utf-8`. Excel may misinterpret non-ASCII characters without a UTF-8 BOM; consider prepending one if customers use Excel.

findings.title: No tests included
findings.explanation: The PR adds a new endpoint with escaping and access-control concerns but no tests. Add tests covering commas/quotes/newlines in kind and payload, formula-leading values, an empty result, an invalid projectId, and unauthorized access.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Add CSV export for project events

Customers asked to download a project's activity log. Adds `GET /projects/:projectId/events.csv`, which returns the latest 10,000 events as CSV. Same query as the JSON events endpoint, larger limit.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/routes/projects.ts b/src/routes/projects.ts
index c30f46c..b019274 100644
--- a/src/routes/projects.ts
+++ b/src/routes/projects.ts
@@ -49,3 +49,18 @@ projectsRouter.delete('/:projectId', async (req, res) => {
   await pool.query('UPDATE projects SET archived_at = now() WHERE id = $1', [projectId])
   res.status(204).end()
 })
+
+projectsRouter.get('/:projectId/events.csv', async (req, res) => {
+  const projectId = Number(req.params.projectId)
+  const { rows } = await pool.query(
+    'SELECT id, kind, payload, created_at FROM events WHERE project_id = $1 ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10000',
+    [projectId],
+  )
+  res.setHeader('content-type', 'text/csv')
+  res.setHeader('content-disposition', `attachment; filename="project-${projectId}-events.csv"`)
+  res.write('id,kind,created_at,payload\n')
+  for (const row of rows) {
+    res.write([row.id, row.kind, row.created_at.toISOString(), JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(row.payload))].join(',') + '\n')
+  }
+  res.end()
+})
```

Report every problem you would raise in a code review, from blocking issues to nits. Respond with only a JSON object, no prose before or after it:

{"findings": [{"file": "path/to/file", "line": <line number in the new version, or null>, "severity": "blocking" | "non-blocking" | "nit", "title": "<short summary>", "explanation": "<why it matters and what to change>"}]}

Use an empty findings list if you would approve the pull request as it is. Write the review in English.
